question: 外貌在多大程度上是一种『资本』？
question_en: How far are looks a form of capital?
sub: 招聘、相亲、镜头前的溢价是真的；可同一把尺，也量得到口音、举止和一本通讯录。
sub_en: The premium in hiring, in dating and on camera is real — but the same measure reaches an accent, a bearing and an address book.

casting.reason: 把成本—收益分析推进到别人认为不该计算的地方——家庭、犯罪、歧视——是他一生的工作。凡是能积累、会折旧、带来可测回报的东西都该叫资本，外貌不构成例外；而他早年关于歧视的模型给出一个更硬的推论：按偏好而非产出挑人的雇主自己要付代价，竞争会惩罚他。他关心的因此不是这公不公道，而是这笔投资从哪一档开始归零，以及约束究竟落在谁头上。
casting.reason_en: Pushing cost-benefit analysis into the places others thought should not be costed — the family, crime, discrimination — was his life's work. Anything that accumulates, depreciates and yields a measurable return deserves the name capital, and looks are no exception. His early model of discrimination adds a harder claim: an employer who selects by taste rather than by output pays for the privilege, and competition fines him. So his interest is not whether any of this is just, but where the investment stops paying and on whom the constraint actually falls.

casting.reason: 美对男人与对女人从来不是同一件事：男人的外表被当成他这个人的一部分，女人的外表被当成她的全部——在一篇专论女性美的短文里，她把后者称作一种被允许持有的次等权力。她由此拒绝资本这个词：资本可以搁着不投，而这份要求没有辞职权，每天都得重新证明一次。镜头本身也被她放进被告席——影像不只是记录，它改变人看世界与看自己的方式，并在这件事上把工时拉长到全天。
casting.reason_en: Beauty has never been the same thing for men and for women: a man's looks are taken as one part of him, a woman's as the whole of her — and in a short essay specifically on women's beauty she called the latter a permitted, second-class kind of power. That is why she refuses the word capital: capital can be left uninvested, while this demand carries no right of resignation and must be met afresh each day. She puts the camera in the dock as well — images do not merely record, they change how people see the world and themselves, and on this subject they have stretched the working day to cover all of it.

casting.reason: 他测的是判断本身：给人看一张陌生的脸，只闪一百毫秒，可信、能干、强势的分数就已经出来了，再多给时间只让人更笃定、不更准确。同一批评分能预测约七成的国会选举结果，可它与当事人的真实能力几乎不相关。于是溢价的真实与判断的可靠被他拆成两件事——脸上的回报是真的，回报所依据的那份信息是假的。他既不肯说这是无稽之谈，也不肯把它抬举成识人的直觉。
casting.reason_en: What he measures is the judgement itself: flash an unfamiliar face for a hundred milliseconds and the ratings for trustworthiness, competence and dominance are already in; give people longer and they grow more certain without growing more accurate. The same ratings predict around seven in ten congressional races, yet they correlate barely at all with what the person can actually do. He therefore splits two things usually run together — the premium is real, and the information it rests on is false. He will neither dismiss face reading as nonsense nor promote it to intuition about character.

casting.reason: 被相貌与出身判过一次的，正是他自己：初见五祖，被问『汝是岭南獦獠，若为堪作佛』，他答人虽有南北、佛性本无南北。所以他不从公平或回报进入这个问题，而从生起分别的那一念进入——见相即刻取舍，问题不在那张脸，在照见它的那颗心。他也不主张闭眼不看：禅门要的是照而不粘，见妍见媸都不跟着走。
casting.reason_en: Judged once by his own looks and origin, he answered the Fifth Patriarch — who had asked how a southern barbarian could hope to become a Buddha — that people may be of the north or the south while Buddha-nature is of neither. So he enters the question neither through fairness nor through returns but through the instant in which a distinction arises — the trouble is not in the face but in the mind that takes or rejects it on sight. Nor does he counsel shutting one's eyes: Chan asks you to reflect without sticking, and to follow neither the fair nor the plain.

casting.reason: 两套秩序必须分开，这是他一贯的坚持：市场按你带进交换的东西给你定位，那是阶级；另有一套按社会尊荣排座次——谁配与谁同席、谁的举止算得体，那是身份团体。把外貌放进后者，就得出一个不讨喜的推论：它的账本记在别人眼里而不在银行里，所以税收与再分配都够不着。他也提醒程序的射程——法规管得住录取名单，管不住谁在散会后被留下来多聊十分钟。
casting.reason_en: Two orders must be kept apart, and he never lets the point go: the market places you by what you bring to an exchange, and that is class; another order seats people by social honour — who may sit with whom, whose bearing counts as correct — and that is the status group. Put looks in the second and an unwelcome corollary follows: their ledger is kept in other people's eyes rather than at a bank, so neither taxation nor redistribution can reach them. He also marks the range of any procedure — rules can govern a shortlist, but not who is kept back for ten more minutes after the meeting.

casting.reason: 表面在他这里根本不必辩护：美自身即目的，不需兑换成德行或用处才有资格存在。『只有肤浅的人才不以貌取人』是他的话，而那是一句认真的挑衅——要求每位受惠者表演愧疚，社会并不因此变得公正，只是多了一层伪善。他也是这张桌上最不相信程序中立的人：删掉照片，偏见会搬到声音、名字与那件外套上去。
casting.reason_en: Surfaces, in his hands, need no defence at all: beauty is its own end and does not have to be converted into virtue or use in order to be allowed to exist. 'It is only shallow people who do not judge by appearances' is his line, and it is a serious provocation — requiring every beneficiary to perform guilt does not make a society just, it only adds a layer of hypocrisy. He is also the least persuaded at this table that any procedure is neutral: strike the photograph and the prejudice moves to the voice, the name and the coat.

casting.reason: 他用一句话处理天赋：从道德的观点看它们是任意的——你没有做什么去挣得自己的长相。任意不等于必须抹平，他真正追问的是制度要不要把这份任意再乘一次：在无知之幕后面，不知道自己将长什么样的人，会同意让一张照片进入录取流程吗？他因此不反对美，只反对让美越界去做本该由证据做的判断，并把删照片、结构化评分这类枯燥程序看成正义的实际形态。
casting.reason_en: He disposes of natural endowments in a sentence: from a moral point of view they are arbitrary — you did nothing to earn the face you have. Arbitrary does not mean it must be levelled; what he presses is whether institutions should multiply that arbitrariness a second time. Behind the veil of ignorance, not knowing what face you will wear, would you agree to let a photograph enter the hiring process? He does not oppose beauty, then, only beauty crossing over to do work that evidence should do, and he treats dull procedures — blind applications, structured scoring — as what justice looks like in practice.

posts.text: 只有肤浅的人才不以貌取人——这句话我说过，至今不打算收回。诸位把美当成一笔需要辩护的财产，已经先替它认了半个罪。**美不是一笔待征税的收入，它是少数几样不必解释自己为何存在的东西之一。**至于公平：这张桌子真正难忍的不是有人好看，是有人好看而不必道歉。一个社会若要求每位受惠者都表演一遍愧疚，它并没有因此变公正，只是多了一层伪善。
posts.text_en: It is only shallow people who do not judge by appearances — I said that, and I have no plans to take it back. By treating beauty as property in need of a defence, you have already pleaded it half guilty. **Beauty is not income awaiting taxation; it is one of the few things that need not explain why it exists.** As for fairness: what this table finds intolerable is not that some people are beautiful, but that some are beautiful and feel no need to apologise. A society that requires every beneficiary to perform guilt has not thereby become just. It has merely acquired one more layer of hypocrisy.

posts.text: 我和威利斯给受试者看一张陌生面孔，只闪一百毫秒，然后问：可信吗？能干吗？他们给得出答案。再给一秒、一分钟，答案几乎不变，只是更笃定。我们还发现，陌生人仅凭照片打出的能干分，能预测约七成美国国会选举的胜负。**所以颜值红利是真的——真的不是因为脸上写着本事，而是因为所有人在同一瞬间误读了同一张脸。**这些印象多半是过度泛化：把表情与熟悉感读进一张静止的脸。嘴角天生下垂，就被判成不好相处。
posts.text_en: Willis and I showed people an unfamiliar face for a hundred milliseconds and then asked: trustworthy? competent? They had answers. Give them a second, or a minute, and the answers barely move — they only grow more certain. We also found that competence ratings made by strangers from photographs alone predict around seven in ten US congressional races. **So the beauty premium is real — real not because ability is written on a face, but because everyone misreads the same face in the same instant.** Most of these impressions are overgeneralisation: expression and familiarity read into a still face. A mouth that merely turns down at rest is scored as hard to work with.

glossary.过度泛化: overgeneralisation（过度泛化）：把一套本来针对别处的判断规则，套到一个只是长得像的对象上。托多罗夫用它解释面孔印象的来源——我们读一张静止的脸，用的其实是读情绪表情与读熟人面孔的那套规则，于是天生眉压得低的人被当成生气，下垂的嘴角被当成不好相处。

glossary_en.overgeneralisation: Applying a rule of judgement built for one thing to something that merely resembles it. Todorov uses it to explain where face impressions come from: we read a still face with the machinery evolved for reading emotional expressions and familiar faces, so a man with naturally low brows is read as angry and a downturned mouth is read as hard to work with.

posts.text: 经济学不问公不公平，只问价格从哪里来。工资里那截溢价若稳定存在，它就是资本——人力资本的一支：能积累、会折旧、有回报率。我算过歧视的代价：雇主按偏好而不按产出挑人，等于自愿多付一笔钱，竞争会罚他。**把外貌叫作资本不是冒犯，是把一件说不清的委屈翻译成可计算、可配置的东西。**剩下的问题只有一个：这笔投资从哪一档开始递减？睡眠和牙齿很高，第三次动刀接近于零。
posts.text_en: Economics does not ask whether a thing is fair; it asks where the price comes from. If that slice of premium in wages is stable, it is capital — a branch of human capital: it accumulates, it depreciates, it has a rate of return. I once costed out discrimination: an employer who picks by taste rather than by output is volunteering to pay more, and competition fines him for it. **Calling looks capital is not an insult; it translates a grievance nobody can pin down into something you can cost and allocate.** That leaves one question: where does this investment start to fall off? Sleep and teeth are high. A third operation is close to zero.

glossary.人力资本: human capital（人力资本）：贝克尔等人提出的概念，指附着在人身上、能提高其产出与收入的那些可积累存量——教育、技能、健康、经验。它的要点是把原本看似天赋或命运的东西当成投资对象来分析：有成本、有回报率、会折旧，也因此可以问一句『再投下去还值不值』。

glossary_en.human capital: Becker's term for the accumulable stock carried in a person that raises their output and earnings — schooling, skills, health, experience. The point of it is to treat what looks like talent or fate as an object of investment: it has costs, a rate of return and depreciation, which makes it sensible to ask whether the next unit is still worth buying.

posts.text: 请把资本这个词放慢一点。资本可以搁着不投，美对女人从来不是选项，是一份没有辞职权的工作。男人的外表被当作他这个人的一部分，女人的外表被当作她这个人的全部——所以美不是权力，是一种被允许持有的次等权力，**你得每天重新证明自己配得上它，而评委永远不是你。**我写过这重双重绑定：不打理，是失职；打理，是承认自己只剩这个。镜头只是把工时拉长到了全天。
posts.text_en: Slow down on the word capital. Capital can be left uninvested; for a woman, beauty has never been optional — it is work with no right of resignation. A man's looks are taken as one part of him; a woman's are taken as the whole of her. So beauty is not power but a permitted, second-class version of power: **you must prove afresh every day that you deserve it, and the judges are never you.** I have written about this double bind: neglect it and you have failed at your job; attend to it and you concede that it is all you have left. The camera merely stretched the working day to cover all of it.

glossary.双重绑定: double bind（双重绑定）：一种两条指令互相取消的处境——照做错，不照做也错，而且不许指出这个矛盾本身。桑塔格用它描述加在女性外貌上的要求：不修饰会被判为疏懒，修饰又被判为除此之外别无所长，两条路都通向减分。

glossary_en.double bind: A situation in which two demands cancel each other out — you are wrong if you comply and wrong if you do not, and the contradiction itself may not be named. Sontag uses it for the demand placed on women's appearance: to go unadorned is read as negligence, to adorn is read as having nothing else, and both roads lead to a deduction.

posts.text: 诸位在混用两套秩序。市场上决定你位置的是阶级，凭你带进交换的东西；另有一套身份团体，按社会尊荣排座次——谁配与谁同席，谁的举止算得体。**外貌不是阶级资本，是身份荣誉的通行证；所以它躲得过税，也躲得过再分配。**身份秩序的账本记在别人眼里，不记在银行里。这也解释了贝克尔的竞争压力为何迟迟没把溢价磨平：歧视若只是趣味，竞争会罚它；若是尊荣，竞争正忙着替它定价。
posts.text_en: You are running two orders together. Your place in the market is set by class, by what you bring to an exchange. The other order is the status group, seated by social honour — who may sit with whom, whose bearing counts as correct. **Looks are not class capital but a pass into status honour, which is why they slip past taxation and past redistribution alike.** The ledger of a status order is kept in other people's eyes, not at a bank. It also explains why Becker's competitive pressure has been so slow to grind the premium away: if discrimination is merely a taste, competition fines it; if it is honour, competition is busy pricing it.

glossary.身份团体: status group（身份团体，Stände）：韦伯与阶级并列的一套分层。阶级由市场处境决定——你手里有什么可以拿去交换；身份团体由社会尊荣决定——生活方式、举止、通婚与同席的资格。两者常常错开：有钱而不被接纳，或清贫而备受敬重，说的就是一个人在两张榜上的位置不同。

glossary_en.status group: Weber's stratum alongside class. Class is fixed by market position — what you hold that can be taken to an exchange; a status group is fixed by social honour — style of life, bearing, and who may marry or dine with whom. The two often come apart: rich but not received, or poor but widely respected, simply means standing at different heights on the two tables.

posts.text: 先把一件事说清楚：长相在道德上是任意的。你没做什么去挣得它，也没做什么以致失去它，它和生在哪个家庭一样，是自然彩票的结果。任意不等于必须抹平；**真正的问题从来不是谁天生占了便宜，而是制度要不要把这份便宜再乘一次。**无知之幕后面你不知道自己将长什么样，你会同意让招聘官凭一张照片定下名单吗？不会。所以删照片、做结构化面试——这不是压抑美，是不让美代替判断。
posts.text_en: Let us settle one thing first: how you look is morally arbitrary. You did nothing to earn it and nothing to lose it; like the family you were born into, it is an outcome of the natural lottery. Arbitrary does not mean it must be levelled out. **The real question was never who got lucky, but whether institutions should multiply that luck a second time.** Behind the veil of ignorance, not knowing what face you will wear, would you agree to let a recruiter fix the shortlist from a photograph? You would not. So strip the photo and structure the interview — that is not the suppression of beauty, it is keeping beauty from standing in for judgement.

glossary.无知之幕: veil of ignorance（无知之幕）：罗尔斯设计的思想实验。让人在不知道自己将是谁——男女、贫富、健康与否、长什么样——的条件下去选社会规则，因为没法为自己量身定制，选出来的规则才可能公平。它的用处是把『我恰好在哪一边』从判断里剔出去。

glossary_en.veil of ignorance: Rawls's thought experiment. People choose the rules of a society without knowing who they will turn out to be — man or woman, rich or poor, healthy or not, handsome or plain — so that, unable to tailor the rules to themselves, they choose rules that can be fair. Its use is to strip out of the judgement the question of which side you happen to be on.

posts.text: 五祖问我何方人、欲求何物。我答：岭南人，唯求作佛。祖曰：汝是岭南獦獠，若为堪作佛？我对：人虽有南北，佛性本无南北；獦獠身与和尚不同，佛性有何差别？**诸君所论者，水上之纹也；纹有妍媸，水无妍媸。**镜不择物而照：妍者来则妍现，媸者来则媸现，镜未尝动念。见一面而即生取舍，所取所舍者非彼面，乃汝心也。
posts.text_en: The Fifth Patriarch asked where I came from and what I wanted. From Lingnan, I said, and I want only to become a Buddha. He said: you are a southern barbarian, how could you become a Buddha? I answered: people may be of the north or the south, but Buddha-nature is of neither; my barbarian body differs from the master's, but wherein does the Buddha-nature differ? **What you are all discussing is the ripple on the water; a ripple may be fair or ugly, the water is neither.** A mirror does not choose what it reflects: the fair comes and fairness appears, the plain comes and plainness appears, and the mirror has never stirred a thought. A man sees one face and at once takes or rejects — and what he takes or rejects is not that face but his own mind.
posts.vernacular: 五祖问我是哪里人、来求什么。我说：岭南人，只求作佛。他说：你是岭南的獦獠，怎么配作佛？我回答：人虽然分南北，佛性并不分南北；獦獠的身体和和尚的不一样，佛性又有什么差别？**诸位议论的是水面上的纹，纹有美丑，水没有美丑。**镜子不挑东西才照：美的来就现美，丑的来就现丑，镜子从没动过一个念头。人见一张脸就立刻起了取舍，所取所舍的并不是那张脸，是你自己的心。

glossary.佛性: Buddha-nature（佛性）：众生本具的觉悟可能，禅宗尤其强调它人人现成、不因身份出身而增减。慧能答五祖『佛性本无南北』正取此义：南人北人、贵贱妍媸都在相上，佛性不在相上，所以身份差别不构成修行资格的差别。

glossary_en.Buddha-nature: The capacity for awakening said to be already present in every being. Chan insists it is complete in everyone and neither increased nor diminished by birth or standing. Huineng's reply that Buddha-nature is of neither north nor south turns on exactly this: northerner and southerner, high and low, fair and plain are all matters of form, and Buddha-nature is not a matter of form, so no difference of standing makes a difference to one's fitness to practise.

posts.text: 贝克尔先生，你的模型里空着一格：维护。资本可以搁着不动，这一项不能——它每天折旧，而修补的账单只寄给一半人口。更要紧的是回报归谁：**一个女人在脸上花掉的钱和钟点，大部分没有变成她的溢价，变成了别人的营业额。**你说边际回报递减，可那个行业的全部生意，正是让你永远算不清自己在哪一档。这不是投资，是订阅。
posts.text_en: Mr Becker, there is an empty cell in your model: upkeep. Capital can sit still; this cannot — it depreciates daily, and the repair bill is sent to half the population only. What matters more is who collects the return. **Most of what a woman spends on her face, in money and in hours, does not become her premium; it becomes somebody else's revenue.** You say returns diminish at the margin, but the entire business of that industry consists in making sure you can never work out which margin you are on. This is not an investment. It is a subscription.

posts.text: 你说的东西在我的语言里也有：那是约束，不是偏好。一项成本只落在一半人口头上的要求，本来就该当税看，我不否认。但你把一个行业的营销当成了我的模型。**溢价由市场给，账单由产业收，两笔账要分开记，否则你只能劝她别投资，而她明天还得去面试。**可用的结论是：把钱放在有外溢的那几项——睡眠、牙齿、合身的衣服，它们同时抬高健康与议价能力；订阅退掉。
posts.text_en: What you are describing exists in my language too: that is a constraint, not a preference. A requirement whose cost falls on half the population should indeed be read as a tax, and I do not dispute it. But you have mistaken one industry's marketing for my model. **The premium is set by the market and the bill is collected by the industry; keep the two accounts apart, or all you can tell her is not to invest — and she still has an interview tomorrow.** The usable conclusion: put the money into the items with spillovers — sleep, teeth, clothes that fit — which raise health and bargaining power at once. Cancel the subscription.

posts.text: 王尔德先生，我不要求任何人愧疚，我谈的是制度，不是情感。你可以毫无歉意地美，正如有人可以毫无歉意地聪明，这两样我都不打算征收。**但因美而被欣赏是一回事，因美而拿到职位、贷款与陪审团的好感是另一回事。**前者属于趣味，后者是把自然彩票的结果换成了对基本益品的支配权。我反对的不是美，是让美越过界去做判断的活。
posts.text_en: Mr Wilde, I ask no one to feel guilty; my subject is institutions, not sentiments. You may be beautiful without apology, as others are clever without apology, and I propose to levy neither. **But being admired for your looks is one thing, and getting the post, the loan and the jury's goodwill from them is another.** The first belongs to taste; the second converts an outcome of the natural lottery into command over primary goods. What I oppose is not beauty but beauty crossing the line to do the work of judgement.

glossary.基本益品: primary goods（基本益品）：罗尔斯用来衡量一个人处境好坏的清单——权利与自由、机会、收入与财富、以及自尊的社会基础。它的用意是避开『谁过得更幸福』这种无法比较的争论，只问每个人手里握着多少这类人人都用得上的通用手段。

glossary_en.primary goods: Rawls's list for measuring how well or badly a person is placed — rights and liberties, opportunities, income and wealth, and the social bases of self-respect. The point is to sidestep the unanswerable argument about whose life feels happier and ask only how much each person holds of the all-purpose means that anyone would want.

posts.text: 越界？亲爱的罗尔斯先生，是美先到，你的表格后到。**删掉照片并不曾消灭偏见，只是把它挪去了第二页——声音、名字、握手，还有那件外套。**我并不反对你的程序，我只请你别把它当中立来宣传：表格能让偏见慢下来，却请不出房间。人总得凭点什么去信一个陌生人；你能做的是让判断慢一点、材料多一点，而不是假装自己没有眼睛。至于那些被你的程序挡在外面的东西，它们并不会消失，只会换个名字再进来一次。
posts.text_en: Crossing the line? My dear Rawls, beauty arrived first and your form came later. **Striking out the photograph has abolished no prejudice; it has merely moved it to the second page — the voice, the name, the handshake, and that coat.** I have nothing against your procedure. I only ask you not to advertise it as neutral: a form can slow prejudice down, it cannot see it out of the room. A person must trust a stranger on the strength of something; what you can do is make the judgement slower and better fed, not pretend you have no eyes. As for whatever your procedure keeps outside, it does not vanish — it comes back in under another name.

posts.text: 贝克尔，我要挑你最硬的那句：竞争会罚掉歧视。我的数据不同意。若溢价来自真实产出，竞争确会把它对齐；可我们测到的能干感与实际表现相关极弱，误判本身却高度一致。**当所有人错得一模一样，市场不会纠正这个错，只会把它定价成常识。**这就是长相溢价能稳稳待在工资方程里一百年的原因：它不是趣味，是一种共享的知觉错误，没有哪个套利者能靠反向下注赚到钱。
posts.text_en: Becker, I want your hardest sentence: competition fines discrimination. My data disagree. If the premium tracked real output, competition would indeed align it; but the perceived competence we measure correlates very weakly with actual performance, while the error itself is strikingly uniform. **When everyone is wrong in precisely the same way, a market does not correct the error — it prices it as common sense.** That is how a looks premium has sat in wage equations for a century: it is not a taste but a shared perceptual error, and no arbitrageur can make money betting the other way.

glossary.套利: arbitrage（套利）：在同一样东西被两处定价不同的时候低买高卖，赚取差价，而这个动作本身会把差价抹平。市场有自我纠错能力的说法就建立在它之上——前提是有人看得出定价错了。托多罗夫的反驳正是针对这个前提：若所有人错得一样，就没有人处在能套利的位置上。

glossary_en.arbitrage: Buying where a thing is cheap and selling where it is dear, an act that erases the gap it feeds on. The claim that markets correct themselves rests on it — provided someone can see that the price is wrong. Todorov's objection goes to exactly that proviso: if everyone is wrong in the same way, nobody is standing where the arbitrage could be made.

posts.text: 罗尔斯，你的程序管得住科层制那一段，管不住它之外。**你可以立法规定谁被录取，你没法立法规定谁被邀请、谁被记住、谁在散会后被留下来多聊十分钟。**身份荣誉恰恰是在这些不写进合同的地方分配的。所以我对删照片没有异议，只提醒它的射程：表格之内你赢，表格之外这笔资本照样流转，而且流得比工资快。
posts.text_en: Rawls, your procedure governs the bureaucratic stretch and nothing outside it. **You can legislate who gets hired; you cannot legislate who gets invited, who is remembered, and who is kept back for ten more minutes after the meeting.** Status honour is distributed precisely in the places that never enter a contract. So I have no objection to striking the photograph — I only note its range. Inside the form you win. Outside it, this capital circulates as before, and it moves faster than wages do.

posts.text: 王尔德言：人必凭所见以信人。此言得其半。**见色相非病，见而即断、断而不疑，乃是病。**汝谓不能无眼。然见花而知花，见人便谓知其人，是以眼代心。禅门不教人闭目，教人识取念起之处。念起而知，是谓自在；念起而随，是谓被缚。红尘中尽可照面，照而不粘，斯可矣。
posts.text_en: Wilde says a man must trust by what he sees. That is half true. **Seeing form is not the sickness; seeing and deciding at once, deciding and never doubting — that is the sickness.** You say you cannot be without eyes. But to see a flower and know a flower, then see a person and claim to know the person, is to let the eye stand in for the mind. Chan does not teach you to shut your eyes. It teaches you to catch the place where a thought starts. A thought arises and you know it: that is freedom. A thought arises and you follow it: that is bondage. Meet as many faces as the world brings — reflect them and do not stick.
posts.vernacular: 王尔德说，人总得凭看见的去信人。这话只对了一半。**看见相貌不是病，一看见就立刻下判断、判断完再不怀疑，才是病。**你说你不能没有眼睛。可是看见花知道是花，看见人就说自己懂了这个人，这是拿眼睛代替了心。禅门不教人闭眼，教人认出念头起来的那个地方。念头起来你知道，叫自在；念头起来你跟着走，叫被绑住。在红尘里照样与人打照面，照见了别粘上去，就可以了。

posts.text: 三轮下来我改一处、留两处。改的是：托多罗夫说服了我——判断本身若系统性出错，竞争不会自动纠正，得靠改流程把那条信息压掉，那是制度的活。留的是：第一，叫它资本仍然对，因为你能算、能配置、能止损；第二，回报曲线陡峭地掉下去。**给普通人的算法只有一句：先买那些同时也买到健康的东西，到此为止，余下的预算投进技能。**牙齿、睡眠、体重、一套合身的衣服，这四样的回报远高于之后的任何一笔；至于把脸改到第几版，边际收益早已归零，风险不会。
posts.text_en: Three rounds in, I change one thing and keep two. The change: Todorov has convinced me that where the judgement itself is systematically wrong, competition will not correct it on its own — you have to redesign the process so the information is suppressed, and that is institutional work. What stands: first, capital is still the right word, because you can cost it, allocate it and cut your losses; second, the return curve falls away steeply. **The whole algorithm for an ordinary person is one line: buy the items that also buy you health, stop there, and put the rest of the budget into skills.** Teeth, sleep, weight and one suit that fits return far more than anything bought after them. As for which version of your face comes next, the marginal gain is already zero, and the risk is not.

posts.text: 我接受韦伯关于射程的批评：程序管得住表格，管不住饭桌。但这不构成放弃程序的理由，只说明它需要补。可做的有三件：招聘删掉照片与姓名；面试统一问题、统一评分；把谁被邀请也写进记录——被记录的分配才可能被争论。**检验一项制度的标准不是它有没有消灭运气，而是它有没有把运气再乘一遍。**至于个人：你选不了自己的脸，但在归你决定的那几次录取、提名与引荐里，你可以不让一张脸替你做判断。
posts.text_en: I accept Weber's criticism about range: procedure governs the form, not the dinner table. That is no reason to abandon procedure, only a reason to supplement it. Three things can be done: strip photographs and names from applications; run every interview on the same questions and the same scoring; and put who gets invited into the record as well — a distribution that is recorded is a distribution that can be argued over. **The test of an institution is not whether it has abolished luck, but whether it has multiplied luck a second time.** As for individuals: you cannot choose your face, but in the few hirings, nominations and introductions that are yours to decide, you can refuse to let a face decide for you.

posts.text: 把我的结论压成两句：印象在一百毫秒里成形、人人一致；它对一个人究竟如何几乎没有预测力。两句要一起用。**别人对你的第一印象不是关于你的信息，而是关于一张脸的几何。**能做的很朴素：第一印象拦不住，但会被后续证据覆盖，所以能多见一次就多见一次，能让对方先看作品就别只让他看脸。若你是做决定的那一方，把判断推到第二份材料之后——**你并不比我的受试者更准，只是更笃定。**
posts.text_en: Compress my findings into two sentences: impressions form within a hundred milliseconds and everybody agrees on them; and they predict almost nothing about who a person actually is. The two are only useful together. **Another person's first impression of you is not information about you; it is information about the geometry of a face.** What can be done is plain: a first impression cannot be stopped, but later evidence overwrites it, so take the second meeting wherever you can get one, and let people see the work before they see the face. If you are the one deciding, hold the judgement until the second piece of evidence — **you are no more accurate than my subjects were, only more certain.**

posts.text: 最后我只说一件事：别把外貌单拎出来受审，它不过是身份荣誉这一长排里最显眼的一格。同一把尺还量得到口音、餐桌上的举止、面对官僚时的从容、一本通讯录——它们更贵，也藏得更深。**钱能被征税是因为钱看得见；尊荣躲开再分配，不是因为它神圣，是因为它没有计量单位。**所以我给普通人的建议是把力气从最贵的那格挪到可迁移的几格：把话说清楚、准时到、记住别人的名字、该开口时开口。它们同属身份秩序，却不看脸，而且学得会。
posts.text_en: One last thing: do not put looks in the dock on their own. They are merely the most conspicuous cell in a long row of status honour. The same measure reaches an accent, manners at a table, ease in front of an official, an address book — all of them dearer than a face and far better hidden. **Money can be taxed because money can be seen; honour escapes redistribution not because it is sacred but because it has no unit of account.** So my advice to an ordinary person is to move your effort from the most expensive cell to the transferable ones: say things clearly, arrive on time, remember people's names, speak when it is your turn. They belong to the same status order, they do not look at your face, and they can be learned.

posts.text: 我不劝任何人放弃好看，那不过是另一种苛刻。我只要求换掉一个词：这不是资本，是工时。**一件事你不做要扣分、做了不加分，它就不是投资，是无偿劳动。**判断标准也随之换掉：不是这笔钱值不值，而是我停下来会怎样。本周可以做一次实验——挑一个场合，按最省事的方式出现，记下真实的后果。多数人会发现代价小于想象；而那些代价确实大的场合，你至少看清了是谁在收这笔费用。
posts.text_en: I will not tell anyone to give up being beautiful; that is merely another kind of severity. I ask for one word to be replaced: this is not capital, it is hours worked. **When a thing costs you points if you skip it and earns you none if you do it, it is not an investment but unpaid labour.** The test changes with the word: not is this worth the money, but what happens if I stop. Run the experiment this week — pick one occasion, turn up in the least effortful way available, and write down what actually followed. Most people find the cost smaller than they feared; and where the cost really is large, you have at least seen clearly who is charging it.

glossary.无偿劳动: unpaid labour（无偿劳动）：被社会当作理所当然、因而不计入报酬也不计入工时的那部分工作，家务、照料与维持体面都在其列。它的标志不是轻松，而是只被扣分、不被加分：做到了无人提起，没做到立刻有人看见。

glossary_en.unpaid labour: The work a society takes for granted and therefore counts neither in pay nor in hours — housework, caring, and keeping up appearances among them. Its mark is not that it is easy but that it can only lose you points: done, it goes unmentioned; left undone, it is noticed at once.

posts.text: 诸位花了三轮讨论怎样让世界别看脸，可世界还是会一直看下去。我给一条实际得近乎可笑的建议：**与其把美当成要辩护的特权或要偿还的债，不如把它当一门手艺——手艺的意思是它可以被做好，也可以被拿去做别的事。**穿得像你自己，而不是像你害怕的那位评委；把审美花在你的房间、你的句子、你端上桌的那盘菜上。美一旦从脸上分散开，它就不再是谁的资本，也不再是谁的伤口。至于愧疚，还给写它的人。
posts.text_en: You have spent three rounds on how to stop the world looking at faces, and the world will go on looking. My advice is practical to the point of absurdity: **rather than treat beauty as a privilege to be defended or a debt to be repaid, treat it as a craft — which means it can be done well, and it can be turned to other objects.** Dress like yourself and not like the judge you are afraid of; spend your taste on your rooms, your sentences, the dish you put on the table. Once beauty is distributed away from the face it stops being anybody's capital, and stops being anybody's wound. The guilt I return to whoever wrote it.

posts.text: 诸君所争者三：一曰利，二曰不平，三曰身不由己。此三者吾不与诸君争，只添一问：汝临镜时，所忧者相耶？忧者谁耶？**相有生灭，见相者无生灭；认相为己，是以刹那作终身。**然吾不劝弃镜：镜可照容，亦可照心。日间见人而心先分高下，识得此念即可，不必责己——一念能知，便是修行。行住坐卧，皆作此课。久之，见相而心不随，则妍媸由他，而汝自由。
posts.text_en: You argue over three things: gain, injustice, and having no choice. I will not contest any of the three. I add one question only: when you stand before a mirror, is it the form that troubles you, or who it is that is troubled? **Forms arise and pass; the one who sees them does not. Take the form for yourself and you have made an instant into a whole life.** Yet I do not tell you to throw the mirror away: a mirror can show a face and it can show a mind. When you meet someone today and your mind ranks them before a word is spoken, it is enough to recognise that thought — there is no need to blame yourself, for to know a thought as it rises is already the practice. Walking, standing, sitting, lying down, make it your exercise. In time you will see the form and the mind will not follow; then let fair and plain be as they are, and you are free.
posts.vernacular: 诸位争的是三件事：一是利，二是不公，三是身不由己。这三件我都不跟诸位争，只添一问：你照镜子的时候，忧的是那个相，还是那个在忧的人？**相有生有灭，能看见相的那个不生不灭；把相认作自己，就是拿一刹那当一辈子。**但我不劝你把镜子扔了：镜子能照脸，也能照心。白天见了人，心里先分出高低，认出这个念头就够了，不必责怪自己——一念能知，就是修行。走着、站着、坐着、躺着，都可以做这功课。久了，见了相而心不跟着走，美的丑的都由它，你就自由了。

summaries.summary: 溢价是真的，这一点全场没有一个人否认：招聘、相亲、镜头前都有，托多罗夫把它追到一百毫秒的判断里，贝克尔把它写进工资方程。共识还往下走了一层——这笔好处的分配从来不在当事人手里，它由看的人、由流程、由行业一起决定。**争的其实不是外貌值不值钱，而是这笔钱该记在谁的账上。**分歧有三处：它算不算资本，贝克尔说能算就算，桑塔格说不能停下的不是资本而是工时；程序有没有用，罗尔斯要删照片，韦伯与王尔德指出表格之外偏见照样流转；以及要不要从判断本身下手——慧能把问题从那张脸挪到了起分别的那一念上。
summaries.summary_en: The premium is real, and not one voice at the table denies it: it shows up in hiring, in dating and on camera, Todorov traces it back to a judgement made in a hundred milliseconds, and Becker writes it into the wage equation. The agreement goes a layer deeper — how that advantage gets distributed was never in the hands of the person who has it, but is settled jointly by the people looking, by the procedure and by an industry. **The argument is not over whether looks are worth money, but over whose ledger the money belongs in.** Three fault lines remain. Is it capital: Becker says anything you can cost is capital, Sontag says a thing you are not free to stop doing is not capital but hours worked. Does procedure help: Rawls would strip the photograph, while Weber and Wilde note that outside the form the prejudice circulates untouched. And should the judgement itself be the target — Huineng moves the question off the face and onto the instant in which a distinction arises.
summaries.insight: 全场把颜值红利当成一笔直接付给脸的钱，劳动经济学拆过它的传导路径，拆出来的东西更有用：那笔溢价里有相当一块并不是雇主盯着脸付的，而是经由自信与说话方式转出去的。被善待着长大的人更敢开口、更敢要价、在面试里更放松，雇主为这些行为付钱，脸只是它们的上游。这也解释了一件怪事：把长相这个变量按住之后，沟通表现仍能吃掉很大一块差距。**于是这笔资本里最大的一块，恰好是可以单独拿出来练的那一块。**对普通人这是个不算小的好消息：脸改不动，敢开口能从今天开始练，而且它在电话里、邮件里、看不见脸的线上会议里照样兑现。
summaries.insight_en: The table treats the beauty premium as money paid directly to a face. Labour economists have taken apart how it travels, and what they found is more useful: a substantial share of that premium is not paid by an employer looking at a face, it is routed through confidence and speech. People treated well from childhood speak up sooner, ask for more, and sit more easily in an interview; employers pay for those behaviours, and the face is only upstream of them. It also explains an oddity — hold looks constant and communication still absorbs a large part of the gap. **Which means the biggest share of this capital is exactly the share you can take out and train on its own.** For an ordinary person that is no small piece of good news: the face cannot be changed, speaking up can be practised starting today, and it pays out over the phone, in email and in meetings where nobody can see your face at all.
summaries.advice: 先把一个小时花在图像上，而不是花在脸上：同一个人的不同照片，可信度评分的差距能和不同人之间一样大，所以认真拍一张光线正、姿势自然的工作照，换掉简历、工牌和资料页上那张随手截的——一次性的成本，覆盖你所有的一次性场合。接着练那条传导路径：把自我介绍压成两句、出声念三遍；下一次开会主动说出第一句话；记住并当面叫出三个人的名字。最后给自己立一条规矩：凡是『我对这个人感觉不对』的判断，都得说得出一条与长相无关的具体理由，说不出就不算数。**你改不了别人怎么看你，但你能决定自己那一票在第几秒落下。**
summaries.advice_en: Start by spending an hour on the image rather than on the face: ratings of trustworthiness vary as much across different photographs of one person as they do across different people, so take one properly lit, naturally posed working photograph and use it to replace the snapshot on your CV, your badge and your profile — a one-off cost that covers every one-off occasion you will ever have. Then train the route the premium travels: compress your self-introduction into two sentences and say them aloud three times; speak the first sentence at the next meeting; learn three people's names and use them to their faces. Finally, set yourself a rule: any verdict of the form 'something about this person feels off' has to come with one concrete reason that has nothing to do with looks, and without one it does not count. **You cannot change how others see you, but you can decide at which second your own verdict lands.**

summaries.summary: 外貌会在极短时间触发高度一致的判断，而这些判断往往缺乏对能力与品格的真实预测力；一旦招聘、选举或社交网络把它当作筛选器，自然偶然便会被制度放大。**各方真正共享的结论是：第一印象无法禁止，却不应未经核验就兑换成职位、收入与尊荣。**分歧主要在命名和边界：它究竟是可投资、会折旧的资本，是女性承担的不对称工时，是身份秩序的通行证，还是无需道歉的审美经验？相应的处方也不同：改造流程、控制投入、揭示维护成本、扩散审美，或训练自己见相而不即断。
summaries.insight: 外貌是否构成资本，不能脱离互动结构回答。同一张脸在一次性筛选、短视频和陌生人交易中可能是高杠杆资产；在长期协作、作品可验证和重复交往中，其回报会逐渐让位于可靠性与技能。平台若按点击率分发，还会把微小偏好累积成曝光、机会和收入，形成真正的复利。**关键不是给外貌下一个永久定义，而是找出它在哪个环节成了准入门槛，并让更有预测力的证据先出现。**普通人不必无限升级自己的脸，更值得选择能展示作品、积累口碑、获得复见机会的环境；组织则应同时审计筛选顺序与曝光分配。
summaries.advice: 本周可以做三件事。第一，列出近三个月用于外貌的金钱与时间，分成健康收益、职业基本盘、焦虑订阅三栏；保留睡眠、口腔、清洁和合身衣物，给第三栏设上限。第二，为下一次求职或社交准备一份先证据材料：三项成果、一个作品链接、两句清楚的自我介绍，尽量在见面前送达。第三，当你负责筛人时，先写三条评分标准，再看匿名作品或履历，面谈统一提问并隔夜决定。**最实用的目标不是消灭第一印象，而是延迟它的裁决权。**另选一个低风险场合简化打理，记录真实后果，校准自己对不够好看会怎样的想象。
summaries.summary_en: Appearance elicits rapid, widely shared judgments, yet those judgments often predict actual competence or character poorly. Once hiring, elections, or social networks use them as filters, a morally arbitrary trait is converted into cumulative advantage. **The clearest shared conclusion is that first impressions cannot be abolished, but they should not gain unchecked power over jobs, income, or social standing.** The real disagreement concerns classification and limits. Is appearance an investable asset that depreciates, an unequal burden of maintenance, a passport within a status order, or an aesthetic good that needs no apology? Each framing suggests a different remedy: redesign selection procedures, cap low-return spending, expose unpaid maintenance work, spread aesthetic agency beyond the face, or cultivate awareness of snap judgments without obeying them. These views remain compatible in one practical sense: appearance can be enjoyable and socially consequential at the same time, so protecting beauty as expression does not require allowing it to substitute for evidence where important goods are allocated.
summaries.insight_en: Whether appearance functions as capital depends less on the face itself than on the structure of interaction. In one-shot screening, short-form video, and transactions among strangers, it can have enormous leverage. In repeated collaboration, where work is visible and promises can be checked, reliability and skill usually gain weight. Platforms add another mechanism: ranking by clicks can compound a tiny visual preference into greater exposure, opportunities, and eventually income. **The useful question is not whether appearance is capital forever, but where it becomes a gatekeeper and how stronger evidence can be made to arrive first.** For individuals, this shifts effort away from endless facial optimization and toward settings that display work, build reputation, and allow second encounters. For organizations, anonymizing a résumé is not enough; they should also inspect who receives exposure, invitations, callbacks, and informal sponsorship. The sequence of information matters because whoever survives the first filter gets the chance to prove everything else. That is where small bias becomes durable inequality.
summaries.advice_en: Try three small interventions this week. First, audit the last three months of appearance-related money and time. Sort each item into health benefit, professional baseline, or anxiety subscription. Keep sleep, dental care, hygiene, and well-fitting clothes; set a hard cap on the third category. Second, prepare evidence that can precede your face in the next application or introduction: three concrete results, one work sample, and a two-sentence description of what you do. Send it before the meeting when possible. Third, when selecting other people, write three criteria before opening applications, review anonymous work first, ask every candidate the same core questions, and wait overnight before deciding. **The practical aim is not to erase first impressions, but to delay their authority.** Also run one low-stakes experiment: simplify grooming for a routine occasion and record what actually happens. Comparing the observed cost with the feared cost helps distinguish real local norms from a maintenance burden sustained mainly by anticipation.

summaries.summary: 无论是神经知觉的自动化反应，还是劳动力市场的溢价与身份区隔，所有人都承认外貌确实在深刻且非理性地左右着资源分配。争论的关节点在于**它究竟是一种可以主动配置的资产，还是一张必须被制度遏制的天然负债**。贝克尔与托多罗夫关注溢价机制与认知误读的边界，桑塔格与罗尔斯直击其性别剥削与分配正义缺陷；韦伯将其归为无法以货币清算的社会尊荣，而王尔德与慧能则分别从审美自足与内观解脱抽离了资本叙事。
summaries.insight: 劳动经济学中哈默梅什（Daniel Hamermesh）的实证研究揭示了一个常被忽略的非对称事实：**相较于拔尖容貌带来的「美貌溢价」，跌出常态水准所遭受的「不修边幅惩罚」要严苛且确定得多。** 消费主义擅长诱导普通人去争夺边际收益骤降、风险极高的前5%「容貌金字塔」，但现实社交与职场真正起效的法则是「兜底」而非「冲顶」。外貌资本的本质不是高回报彩票，而是一道基础及格线；只要守住健康与整洁，你就已经拿到了它能给予的绝大部分正向保护。
summaries.advice: 第一，执行贝克尔的「底线止损法」：停止在微调与护肤订阅制上的边际内耗，把预算严格锁死在睡眠、牙齿健康、体态与合身体面的着装上。第二，实践桑塔格的「阻力测试」：本周选一次非关键社交或办公场合，以最省力干净的状态出席，你会发现**预想中的容貌减分在现实中几乎为零**。第三，在担任面试或决策角色时执行托多罗夫与罗尔斯的防御：先盲审文字方案与过往业绩，把看脸的环节推迟到最终验证。
summaries.summary_en: Across neurocognitive heuristics, wage premiums, and social stratification, there is unanimous agreement that appearance profoundly and irrationally dictates the allocation of societal rewards. The critical divide centers on **whether appearance functions as an investable personal asset or as an unearned liability requiring institutional constraint.** While Becker and Todorov dissect the mechanics of wage equations and perceptual errors, Sontag and Rawls target its gendered exploitation and moral arbitrariness. Weber reclassifies it as elusive social honor, whereas Wilde and Huineng abandon the capital paradigm altogether through aesthetic autonomy and detached mindfulness.
summaries.insight_en: Empirical labor economics reveals a crucial asymmetry often lost in public discourse: **the institutional penalty for perceived untidiness is far more severe and consistent than the marginal premium awarded for exceptional beauty.** Commercial culture lures individuals into chasing diminishing returns in the hyper-competitive top percentile, yet real-world markets primarily reward baseline compliance rather than aesthetic perfection. Appearance operates not as a speculative growth asset, but as hygiene factor; securing health, cleanliness, and posture captures almost the entire protective value it has to offer.
summaries.advice_en: First, implement Becker's baseline rule: halt discretionary spending on cosmetic micro-interventions and restrict your budget strictly to sleep, dental care, physical conditioning, and well-fitted clothing. Second, run Sontag's friction test: attend one routine meeting this week using minimal grooming effort to experience firsthand that **the imagined social cost of not over-styling is virtually non-existent.** Third, when evaluating others, adopt Todorov and Rawls's blind protocol by reviewing work samples or portfolios before looking at a candidate's photo or face.

hooks.text: **最贵的那一格没人收**：口音、餐桌上的举止、面对官僚的从容、一本通讯录，都比一张脸贵，也都比一张脸难看见。复制它们几乎不花钱——一次真的引荐，一次改简历。为什么制度只动得了最便宜的那一块？
hooks.text_en: **Nobody levies the dearest cell**: an accent, manners at a table, ease in front of an official, an address book — each dearer than a face and each far harder to see. Copying them costs almost nothing: one real introduction, one CV rewritten. Why can institutions only reach the cheapest part?

hooks.text: **什么时候该经营，什么时候该拒绝**：同一件事，在一次性的短接触里值得做到不扣分，在作品能说话的长期关系里近乎白花钱。判据其实只有一条：这个场合，对方还有没有第二份材料可看。
hooks.text_en: **When to cultivate it, when to refuse the measure**: the same effort is worth spending to avoid a deduction in a one-off encounter and close to wasted in a long relationship where the work speaks. There is really only one test: whether, in this situation, the other person will ever see a second piece of evidence.

answer.lead: 把问题换成一句可操作的：**在这个场合，对方还有没有第二份材料可看？**没有，就打理到不扣分为止；有，就把钱和时间挪到那份材料上。

head: 场合
该怎么做
为什么
rows: 一次性短接触：初面、初次见面、证件照、镜头前
按场合规范打理到不扣分，不追求出彩
判断在百毫秒里成形，而这里没有第二份材料来覆盖它
长期、作品可见的关系：同事、客户、长期合作
把预算从脸挪到作品和第二次见面
后续证据会稳定压过第一印象，继续投在外貌上的回报迅速归零
你是做判断的一方：招聘、评审、引荐
删照片、统一问题、先看作品，判断推迟到第二份材料之后
误判高度一致，市场不会自动纠正，只能靠流程把那条信息压掉
下限项：牙齿、睡眠、体重、整洁、衣服合身
直接做，别犹豫，也别往上加码
惩罚大于奖励：掉到平均线以下要扣的，比升到线以上能加的更多
维持成本明显只落在你这一边：每天数小时、持续花钱
做一次停止实验：挑一个场合按最省事的方式出现，记下真实后果
分辨投资与无偿劳动，唯一的办法是看停下来会怎样

answer.tail: 三条原则：**能被作品覆盖的场合，钱花在作品上**；下限项一次做完就别再加码；判断别人时，把自己的第一眼当成一条待验证的假设，而不是结论。

answer_en.lead: Turn the question into something you can act on: **in this situation, will the other person ever see a second piece of evidence?** If not, groom to the point where nothing is deducted. If so, move the money and the hours onto that evidence.

head: Situation
What to do
Why
rows: One-off, brief contact: a first interview, a first date, an ID photo, being on camera
Meet the local norm well enough to lose no points; do not chase distinction
The judgement forms in a hundred milliseconds and there is no second piece of evidence here to overwrite it
Long-term relationships where the work is visible: colleagues, clients, ongoing partners
Move the budget from the face to the work and to the second meeting
Later evidence reliably outweighs the first impression, and further spending on looks returns almost nothing
You are the one deciding: hiring, reviewing, making introductions
Strip photos, use the same questions, look at the work first, hold judgement until the second piece of evidence
The error is highly uniform, so no market corrects it; only the procedure can suppress the information
Floor items: teeth, sleep, weight, cleanliness, clothes that fit
Do them, without hesitation and without escalating
The penalty outweighs the premium: falling below average costs more than rising above it pays
Upkeep that plainly falls on you alone: hours every day, money on a standing order
Run a stopping experiment: pick one occasion, turn up in the least effortful way, note what actually followed
The only way to tell investment from unpaid labour is to see what happens when you stop

answer_en.tail: Three principles: **where the work can speak, spend on the work**; do the floor items once and stop escalating; and when you judge other people, treat your own first look as a hypothesis awaiting evidence rather than a conclusion.

hooks.text: **账单只寄给一半人**：同一份维持成本，钟点与花费却如此不对称地落在女性身上。把它记成工时而不是投资，劳动法、伴侣之间的分工、公司的着装要求就都得重算一遍。
hooks.text_en: **The bill goes to half the population**: the hours and the money of the same upkeep fall strikingly unevenly on women. Book it as hours worked rather than as investment and labour law, the division of work between partners and a company's dress code all have to be recalculated.

hooks.text: **强制第二眼**：第一印象拦不住，但可以被覆盖。哪些流程能把『先看作品、再见人』写成默认——盲评、样本先行、两次面试之间隔一夜？哪些场合根本补不了第二眼？
hooks.text_en: **Forcing a second look**: a first impression cannot be stopped, but it can be overwritten. Which procedures could make 'work first, person second' the default — blind review, a sample before a meeting, a night between two interviews? And where is a second look simply never available?
